changes: Date year changed from 506 to 509 (ce 1386 → 1389): Bendall's description states N.s. 509 (A.D. 1389). The '५०६' in the transcription is probably an OCR misreading of ५०९, since ६ and ९ are easily confused. 509 also falls within Jayasthitimalla's reign.
Donor name confidence lowered to low (corrupt). Added the title paramasaugata, the probable reading of 'परसीगत'. Separated affiliation (vihāra) from residence.
Purpose reworded as a pious gift (deyadharma) for merit, in place of the quoted formula.
Place: kept the normalization to Patan (Lalitakrama = Lalitapattana; Māṇigala = the Patan palace quarter). The vihāra name was removed from the place string.

date.as_written: सम्वत ५०६ ज्येष्ठशुक्ल दशम्याया तिथौ शुक्रवासरे (Bendall: N. s. 509)

purpose: deyadharma (pious gift) of the donor, merit formula yad atra puṇyaṃ
notes: The transcribed Devanāgarī prints ५०६, but Bendall's description gives N.s. 509 = A.D. 1389. I followed Bendall and took ५०६ as a probable OCR confusion of ९ with ६. Bendall notes that the date and the king's name are in a different, apparently contemporary hand. There is another date inside the cover, probably of a recitation, but it is nearly obliterated. 'मखराजे' stands for 'मल्लराज्ये'. The donor's name 'मलेचजजक' is corrupt, either in the manuscript or in the OCR. 'परसीगत-संध' probably stands for 'paramasaugata-saṃgha'/'paramasaugata'. 'प्रवरमहायानयाचिन' stands for 'pravaramahāyānayāyin'. 'वच्चविहार' may stand for Vatsavihāra; the name is uncertain.
